title: Automation Health cadence-aware stale detection
objective: Replace the universal 36-hour stale threshold for scheduled workflows with deterministic cadence-aware expected-run logic, so valid weekly workflows are not guaranteed to become SCHEDULE_STALE between their legitimate runs while genuinely overdue workflows remain visible.

evidence.summary: Scheduled workflows use a fixed timedelta(hours=36 if cron_count else 192), with no distinction between daily and weekly cron cadence.
The workflow legitimately runs once each Monday at 08:20 Europe/Copenhagen.

The weekly Cycle Navigator calibration loop is marked SCHEDULE_STALE despite a successful scheduled run on Monday 2026-08-24, because the health observation is more than 36 hours later but still before the next legitimate Monday run.
The false weekly stale condition has matured into a CODEX_READY task, proving the observer defect propagates into remediation routing.

forbidden_changes: changing producer workflow schedules to satisfy health
reproduction: Use a valid weekly cron such as 20 8 * * 1 with Europe/Copenhagen timezone. Set latest successful scheduled run to Monday 08:20 and evaluate health on Wednesday or Thursday before the next Monday. Current classify logic uses a fixed 36-hour threshold whenever cron_count is nonzero, so it emits SCHEDULE_STALE even though no expected run has been missed.

positive: A weekly Monday workflow remains non-stale throughout the interval before its next expected Monday run plus a bounded lateness tolerance.
A daily workflow that misses its expected run beyond the same bounded tolerance is classified SCHEDULE_STALE.
Multiple cron entries use the nearest valid expected schedule rather than a fixed hourly threshold.
Timezone-aware schedules remain deterministic across Europe/Copenhagen daylight-saving transitions or are handled with an explicitly documented fail-closed strategy.
negative: A weekly workflow that actually misses the next expected Monday run beyond tolerance must become SCHEDULE_STALE.
Malformed or unsupported cron syntax must not fabricate a healthy cadence; it must surface an explicit observer limitation or conservative finding.
Manual-only workflows must not become scheduled merely because cron-like text appears elsewhere in the YAML.
The repair must not weaken LATEST_RUN_FAILED, REPEATED_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES, stuck-run or lifecycle safety findings.

clean_noop_condition: Fresh main already computes stale status from actual expected cron cadence and the weekly Cycle Navigator calibration loop no longer becomes stale between legitimate weekly runs.
stop_condition: Stop without code changes if the reproduction no longer holds or if solving it would require changing producer schedules instead of observer logic.
escalation_condition: Escalate to FRAMEWORK_OWNER only if cadence-aware observation cannot be implemented within the existing health observer without introducing new framework semantics.
rollback_plan: Revert only the bounded health cadence logic and tests. Preserve producer workflows and historical health artifacts unchanged.
